title: Garden field notes
body:
Before entering the garden, pause to notice the path, the light and the water supply. Write down what is visible so that another visit can begin with a clear record.

Observe the setting

The pot beside the entrance has recently been watered. Its soil is darker than the dry ground nearby. A tree casts a narrow shadow across the path. Mark these positions on a small sketch.

A useful note describes its conditions. A leaf can look different in shade and sunlight. The surface of the soil may feel different from the soil below it. Write down where and when the observation happened.

Leave a question

Return to the same pot on the next walk. Has its position changed? Are the leaves still reaching toward the window? Keep the question without inventing an answer.

At the desk, arrange the notes into cards. Keep the original words and use headings to help readers find their place. A short note can leave space; a longer note can continue on another card.
highlights: A useful note describes its conditions.
Keep the question without inventing an answer.
